doc.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995

title: Learning piano, the family country band and reading music
summary: His father's country band started him playing; he learned from sheet music and read arrangements for Teagarden.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Can you tell us how the lessons you took as a child, what other kind of learning you had to do to become someone who could play with Teagarden and also do solo piano?

Well when I was going to high school, my dad started a little country band. He played the violin by ear. And he got a group together and we used to play country dances and picnics, church picnics, and things like that. And that’s how I started playing it.
So that’s when you got to start to develop your ear for learning songs more by ear than—
Well we’d buy the sheet music. Thirty-five cents a copy. And you’d learn the tunes that way.
Did you learn chord symbols, to read from chord symbols at that time?
No I just read from the music. The chord symbols above it, I didn’t pay any attention. I think it was for the guitar player or something.
Yeah. But when you went with Teagarden, there had to be a certain amount of playing by—
Arrangements. He had a big band. And that’s what the piano player did, hopefully.
So it really was important to be able to read.
Oh, yeah, well I did that from the beginning you know.
